senses.gloss: ch. sameto stretch, stretch forth; to straighten.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Genesis 22:10">Targ. Y. Gen. XXII, 10</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 31:19">Targ. Prov. XXXI, 19</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 26:18">Ib. XXVI, 18</cite>, v. <cite ref="B01354"><he>בְּשַׁט</he></cite>.—

<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 26b:12">R. Hash. 26ᵇ</cite> <he>כמה דפָשֵׁיט איניש וכ׳</he> the more man straightens his mind (removes all duplicity, v. <cite ref="Q02063">preced.</cite>), the better it is, opp. <he>כייף</he> bends, humbles.—Part. pass. <he>פָּשִׁיט</he>; f. <cite ref="Q02072"><he>פְּשִׁיטָא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Exodus 26:28">Targ. Y. Ex. XXVI, 28</cite> (ed. Amst. <he>פַּשִּׁיט</he>). Targ. II Esth. V, 1.
<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Numbers 23:24">Targ. Y. II, Num. XXIII, 24</cite>.—
<cite ref="Pesachim 113a:3">Pes. 113ᵃ</cite> <he>פְּשׁוֹט</he>; <cite ref="Bava Batra 110a">B. Bath. 110ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="N00589"><he>נְטַשׁ</he> I</cite>.

senses.gloss: (neut. verb) to be stretched forth, reach out.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 8:8:12">Y. Peah VIII, end, 21ᵇ</cite> <he>ידיה דלא פַשְׁטַן מיתן וכ׳</he> may these hands which did not reach out to give thee, be cut off.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 17:3">Gen. R. s. 17</cite> <he>הוון יתבין פַּשְטִין וכ׳</he> he and R. … sat teaching; <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 34">Lev. R. s. 34</cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 18b:2">B. Mets. 18ᵇ</cite> <he>וקא פשיט רבא דיחזיר</he> and Raba decided that restitution must be made.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 9b:2">Kidd. 9ᵇ</cite> <he>בתר דבעיא הדר פַּשְׁטָהּ</he> after having raised the question, he met it again himself.
<cite ref="Berakhot 2b:4">Ber. 2ᵇ</cite> <he>והדר פשטו לה מברייתא</he> and then they solved the question by deduction from a Boraitha.
<cite ref="Horayot 13b:14">Hor. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>פ׳ גרס ותנא וכ׳</he> he explained (the subject to himself), and committed it to memory again and again.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 90b:7">B. Mets. 90ᵇ</cite> <he>פְּשׁוֹט מהא חדא</he> derive from this (Boraitha) one answer to the questions before us.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 25a:2">Kidd. 25ᵃ</cite> <he>מי בעיתו … ולא פְשִׁיטְנָא לכו</he> did you ever ask me anything that I did not explain to you?; a. fr.—V. <cite ref="Q02072"><he>פְּשִׁיטָא</he></cite>.
